title: Record Lifecycle and Editing
summary: Documents edit lifecycle, field-level expectations, and safe change controls for record updates.
coverage: Edit mode behavior and save/cancel flows
Open ports, maintainer, owner, and application fields

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Record edits affect operational ownership, security context, and exported reporting data. Validate values before save, especially for owner, maintainer, and open ports fields.

sections.title: Edit lifecycle contract
paragraphs: Record editing follows an explicit lifecycle: enter edit mode, modify allowed fields, save or cancel, then re-validate from refreshed data. This pattern prevents ambiguous write state and supports predictable audit behavior.
If save succeeds, RAPTOR refreshes the dataset and reorders records by latest modification time. If save fails, the current edit state is preserved so the operator can correct and retry.

sections.title: Editable field contract
paragraphs: The record edit form focuses on fields that drive accountability and technical context. Populate these fields precisely and avoid free-form values that cannot be consistently interpreted by other teams.

rows: Leaving unassigned when service ownership is known.
Business owner or accountable service owner.
Team alias with no accountable person.
Technical maintainer who performs implementation changes.
Copying business owner when maintenance is handled elsewhere.
Externally visible ports in consistent comma-separated format.
Mixed prose like `web ports and admin maybe 8443`.

sections.title: Owner versus maintainer
paragraphs: The owner and maintainer fields serve different operational responsibilities. Conflating them weakens escalation flow and delays incident response.
Owner identifies who is accountable for risk acceptance and business prioritization. Maintainer identifies who is expected to execute technical change and remediation implementation.

rows: Product, service management, or business owner.
SRE, platform engineering, or app engineering.

sections.title: Delete operation and safeguards
paragraphs: Record deletion is a privileged action and should be used only when the asset is out of scope or entered incorrectly. Deletion changes operational visibility and can alter downstream reporting and security workload scope.
Always validate the record identity and confirm retirement status with the owning team before deletion.

tip.title: TIP
paragraphs: Prefer metadata correction over deletion when the record still represents a real service endpoint.

sections.title: Post-edit validation
paragraphs: After each save, validate that assignment, ownership, and open ports reflect intended values. Then verify the record appears correctly in grouped and filtered views.
For critical records, open the detailed record view to review historical updates and ensure changes align with expected operational timeline.
orderedList: Re-open the edited record card after refresh and confirm values.
Run a targeted filter query to verify discoverability by key fields.
Confirm application grouping placement is correct.
If ownership changed, notify downstream security stakeholders.
